text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Finnish bus transporting Silja Line passengers came off road in Sweden, injuring 15 Swedes and four Finns.
- Institutions for care of elderly will have to expand by 20,000 beds by the year 2010, says researcher at the National Research and Development Centre for Welfare and Health (Stakes).

- Finnish jobless benefits to be tightened at the turn of the year. Ten months required for income-related benefit, which will still be paid for 500 days. Level of income-related benefits will be based on last wage but can be no less than 80 percent of previous benefit.
- Finland shelves plan to introduce quotas for men in teachers' training.

- Finnish firms popular investments for foreigners, mainly Swedish and U.S. firms, although fewer foreign acquisitions this year than last, Invest in Finland Bureau says. But direct investment soared to 5.7 billion markka from 2.7 billion.
- Only 13 percent of Finns have never experienced depression and the worst time of the year is autumn when almost half the population is depressed, survey shows.
- The labour market has been made flexible enough and employers should now take responsibility of employment, says chairwoman of parliament's economic committee Tuulikki Hamalainen.
- Finnish local governments say their main concern this year has again been tight budgets.
- Increasing popularity of snow-boarding brings new customers to Finland's ski resorts which see chances to reach top results this season.
- Alcohol makes the brain want nicotine, fresh U.S. study shows.
